A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LongVT study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and reward ablations, contamination probes, inference latency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, revises several reported scores and adds descriptive analysis of VideoMMMU question composition.

M1.justification: The global-to-local crop_video procedure, SFT–RL–RFT pipeline, reward components and trajectory filtering remain unchanged. Clarifications about latent grounding abilities and external tool execution document the existing method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training sources, four long-video QA benchmarks and Charades-STA grounding evaluation. VideoSIAH-Eval deduplication preserves the 244 videos and represented tasks; it changes the reported sample count rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the main accuracy table, contamination probes and latency comparison. Newly cited methods such as Ego-R1, SV Agent and ParaVT are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 changes VideoSIAH-Eval from 1,280 entries to 652 unique QA pairs. A new footnote attributes this to removing approximately uniform export duplicates. Training budgets and frame-sampling regimes remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 2 adds an option-count analysis to the existing contamination study: 286/300 comprehension questions and 279/300 perception questions have ten options, contextualizing blind accuracy against approximately 10–16% chance performance. Existing ablations, reflection analysis, efficiency measurements and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added chance-level discussion does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes dense Qwen2.5-VL's VideoMMMU perception score from 56.7 to 54.7. The contamination table changes adaptation No Visual/Rearranged Choices scores from 25.7/29.7 to 27.0/31.6 for Qwen2.5-VL and from 33.7/36.3 to 35.1/38.7 for Qwen3-VL. Its new MCQ-only note prevents assuming these are same-setting gains. LongVT scores and latency results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SFT loss, GRPO objective and reward definitions are mathematically unchanged. Section 3.2 reverses both the clip argument convention and its stated interval definition, preserving the same operation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction's third contribution now claims first systematic validation that the joint answer-temporal reward and RFT each provide gains over SFT and RL alone. The central framework, dataset and performance claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies that grounding capabilities are activated through training and that 'native' refers to the learned invocation policy despite external crop execution. It adds chance-level reasoning for suspected VideoMMMU memorization and removes the sequence-level reward rationale preceding RFT. Context-window limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New disclosures describe deterministic pixel-level scene detection, specify MCQ-only adaptation evaluation in the contamination table, and explain the benchmark export error and availability of its cleaned version. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompt templates and code location are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds MMR1, Ego-R1, pre-alignment distillation, SV Agent and ParaVT, extending discussion of training transitions and multi-agent video reasoning. The main positioning against VITAL remains. Publication and bibliographic updates largely refer to existing works.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language edits, condenses the RFT and framework explanations, resets supplementary numbering, and updates authorship, contacts and acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The framework diagram moves from main Figure 4 to supplementary Figure 3. Tables are repositioned, supplementary figures and tables are renumbered, and captions and result highlighting receive limited edits. Existing plots, diagrams and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by disclosing benchmark duplication, reporting the unique sample count and clarifying native tool use. Added option-count context also helps interpret the contamination probes. The benefit is limited: most evidence is unchanged, and Table 2 retains a 46.0 Qwen2.5-VL average despite revised displayed scores averaging approximately 45.6.
